subject: CardinalPay - sustained queueing & OOMs on reserved pool (urgent)
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cardinalpay.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cardinalpay.com; support@cardinalpay.com
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 02:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency and errors from reserved pool — production impact

Jonas / Marissa,

We're seeing sustained token-queueing and intermittent OOMs against our reserved capacity for the last 45 minutes. Latency has jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s p90 and we're seeing a ~3% 500 error spike impacting checkout authorization calls. This is impacting live transactions — we have partial degradation across two regions (us-west, us-east).

What we need right now:
- Immediate confirmation that CardinalPay's reserved pool is not being throttled/oversubscribed by other tenants.
- If it's a software fallback or kernel regression, we need an ETA for a mitigation.
- A concise summary for our execs on impact and mitigation steps so we can provide an update to our COO.

I've attached the token queue dump and the spike graph. Please escalate internally — this is P1 for us.

Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, CardinalPay

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 09:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Severe latency and errors from reserved pool — production impact

Lena — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're pulling the on-call infra and runtime owners into this. Preliminary check: reserved pool tokens look within expected allocation but we are seeing sustained request queuing on several nodes and two GPU hosts reporting transient OOM restarts.

Immediate actions from our side (in-progress):
- (Jordan) spinning a hot-standby routing to move CardinalPay traffic to alternate headroom within the same capacity class.
- (Marcus) collecting kernel/runtime logs + GPU telemetry to determine if a recent kernel selection change caused increased memory pressure.
- (Jonas) opening a PagerDuty incident and notifying the exec duty channel.

I'll follow up in 30 minutes with concrete mitigation and whether we need to request short-term burst capacity.

Jonas Weber
Account Lead — Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: lena.ortiz@cardinalpay.com
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Severe latency and errors from reserved pool — production impact

Quick status update from infra:
- Hot-standby routing applied for 30% of CardinalPay traffic. Early telemetry shows p90 latency for routed traffic back to baseline (~140ms).
- Two nodes (gpu-node-18, gpu-node-19) experienced kernel-level OOMs; both restarted and rejoined the pool. We suspect a compaction path in the optimized attention kernel increased peak memory for long-sequence requests.
- I've applied a temporary kernel override to force the prior memory-conservative kernel for CardinalPay's model route. That should eliminate the OOM class while we validate.

Remaining asks for the customer:
- Can CardinalPay provide a short sample of the long-sequence traffic that triggered the compaction (we've received the perf_dump but need sanitized sample prompts to reproduce reliably)?
- If degradation persists after the override, we should plan a controlled fallback to a slightly lower-capacity quantized variant to cap peak memory per-request.

I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to runbook lead if we see any repeat OOMs.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: cardinal_sla_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: lena.ortiz@cardinalpay.com; jordan.blake@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 15:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Severe latency and errors from reserved pool — production impact

Lena — short exec-ready summary and next steps for CardinalPay's COO: 

Summary (one-liner): 
CardinalPay experienced a P1 degradation between 09:10–10:20 UTC due to GPU headroom pressure and transient OOMs on two reserved nodes after a kernel selection path increased peak memory for long-sequence requests. The majority of customer traffic was restored via hot-standby routing and a kernel override; full stabilization was achieved by 10:20 UTC.

Impact: 
- p90 latency increased to ~1.8s for 45 minutes for ~12% of requests; overall 500 error rate peaked at ~3% impacting checkout flows.
- No data exposure; no requests dropped without processing — retries were enforced by the customer's client.

Root cause hypothesis: 
- A recent runtime kernel selection favored a faster but memory-hungry attention implementation for long sequences. Under sustained long-sequence workload, two GPU processes OOMed and restarted, producing queueing while workload redistributed.

Mitigations taken: 
- Applied hot-standby routing (30%) to alternate headroom within the reserved capacity class.
- Forced memory-conservative kernel for CardinalPay's model to prevent further OOMs.
- Collected full telemetry and live perf dump (attached).

Next steps / ask of CardinalPay: 
1) Share a small set of sanitized long-sequence requests to reproduce locally (security-safe).
2) Approve short-term burst to adjacent reserved pool for 24 hours if needed while we run a longer validation and patch.
3) Schedule a postmortem with our runtime team and CardinalPay's SREs tomorrow (Fri) at 09:00 UTC.

If approval for 24h burst is required, I can fast-track a quote to PM and finance for immediate activation. Jordan and Marcus will stay on the incident until the postmortem.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Lead — Priority Accounts, Redwood Inference
